title: Chroma: Local-First Vector DB for Development

questions.q: Chroma's design is described as the embedded-database lineage of which familiar system?
options: Apache Kafka — distributed message bus
Nginx — reverse proxy with connection pooling
SQLite — in-process, file-based, no separate daemon
Redis — in-memory cache with replication
questions.explain: The chapter maps Chroma directly to SQLite: it runs inside your process, writes to a local directory (chroma.sqlite3 catalog plus HNSW files), and requires no separate daemon.

questions.q: What happens in Chroma if you create a collection with text-embedding-3-small (1536 dims) and later query it with a function returning 768-dim vectors?
options: Chroma raises a ValueError at query time — a dimension mismatch is a hard schema error
The query returns approximate results anyway
Chroma re-embeds the collection automatically
Chroma silently truncates the stored vectors
questions.explain: A dimension mismatch is a hard schema error: Chroma raises a ValueError at query time with no silent reduction, so the embedding function attached to a collection must be treated as a schema constraint.

questions.q: Which statement about Chroma's HNSW parameters is correct?
options: hnsw:construction_ef can be tuned per query; hnsw:search_ef requires a rebuild
hnsw:construction_ef is permanent and requires rebuilding the index to change; hnsw:search_ef can be tuned at query time without rebuilding
Both are fixed forever at collection creation
Both can be changed on the fly without any rebuild
questions.explain: construction_ef is baked into index quality permanently, so poor recall means rebuilding; search_ef is the query-time recall/latency lever that can be tuned without rebuilding.

questions.q: According to the chapter, at roughly what scale does Chroma become the wrong-size tool, and why?
options: Above 10,000 vectors — DuckDB cannot handle larger metadata
Above 500 vectors — the embedded client runs out of connections
There is no limit; Chroma scales horizontally
Above 2M vectors — the HNSW index lives entirely in RAM, so a 2M-vector 1536-dim collection needs ~12 GB for the index alone
questions.explain: The chapter gives 2M vectors as the practical ceiling: the whole HNSW index is RAM-resident and single-node, so memory (e.g., ~12 GB for 2M x 1536 float32 before graph overhead) and no distribution force a graduation.

questions.q: What is Chroma's default embedding function, and what dimensionality does it produce?
options: BAAI bge-large-en-v1.5, 1024 dims
OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, 1536 dims
all-MiniLM-L6-v2 via sentence-transformers, 384 dims
Cohere embed-english-v3.0, 1024 dims
questions.explain: Chroma's default embedding function is all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384 dimensions), which runs locally with no API key; the collection infers its dimension constraint from the first insert.
